scenario.name: Elastic & Mandiant — APT41 (Brass Typhoon): DodgeBox, Call-Stack Spoofing & DUSTPAN Loader
scenario.shortSubtitle: Elastic Security Labs / Mandiant · DLL Side-Loading, Synthetic Stack Frames & ChaCha20 DUSTTRAP
scenario.overview: Imagine a master espionage team that sneaks into an office building wearing the uniform of the built-in crash-report clerk. First, a nimble launcher slips a hidden operative straight into the crash-report desk; next, the operative peels off every security tripwire taped onto the office rulebook and fakes its own hallway footsteps so guards see only normal paperwork; finally, it unpacks sixteen modular espionage gadgets purely inside memory and phones home over a custom double-locked radio. In this scenario (T1620, Elastic & Mandiant, APT41 (Brass Typhoon): DodgeBox, Call-Stack Spoofing & DUSTPAN Loader), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: dUSTPAN Launcher Injects Into Windows Error, then sTEALTHVECTOR Unhooking ntdll.dll, then loading DUSTTRAP’s 16 Plugins in Memory. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering DUSTPAN Launcher Injects Into Windows Error, then STEALTHVECTOR Unhooking ntdll.dll, then Loading DUSTTRAP’s 16 Plugins in Memory, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 8 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: DODGEBOX / DUSTPAN DLL SIDE-LOADING & ENV KEYING
stages.subtitle: Relocated signed binary loads malicious ffmpeg.dll and validates host key
stages.description: Rather than walking the halls under its own name, the initial launcher starts the building's built-in crash-reporting clerk and quietly slips a sleeper helper directly into that trusted clerk's workspace. The initial persistence trigger executes the DUSTPAN stage-1 loader (a lightweight launcher documented by Mandiant that contains zero C2 domains or post-exploitation tools of its own, so if an analyst captures the file on disk they learn nothing about the final implant). DUSTPAN immediately spawns C:\Windows\System32\wermgr.exe (Windows Error Reporting Manager, documented by Trend Micro’s Earth Freybug research as chosen because wermgr.exe is a Microsoft-signed binary that legitimately connects to external HTTPS servers to upload crash reports, allowing C2 traffic to blend in) and injects its decryption stub into wermgr.exe’s memory. By immediately transferring execution into C:\Windows\System32\wermgr.exe via remote memory allocation and APC/thread hijacking, all subsequent stages execute under the process identity and digital signature of a built-in Windows telemetry binary. In the documented Sysmon EID 7 exchange from APT41 Cloudflare Worker C2 to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK Unsigned DLL (confirming that the SIDELOAD DODGEBOX request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 CALL-STACK SPOOFING & REFLECTIVE DUSTTRAP MAPPING). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SIDELOAD DODGEBOX / ⇠#1 ACK Unsigned DLL) from Node ① (#1 APT41 Cloudflare Worker C2) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Elastic Defend & ETW Ti Sensor).

stages.title: CALL-STACK SPOOFING & REFLECTIVE DUSTTRAP MAPPING
stages.subtitle: Synthesizing legitimate unwind frames via RtlLookupFunctionEntry before syscall
stages.description: Inside the crash-report clerk desk, the next-stage stealth module temporarily unlocks the core system rulebook to replace tampered security tripwires with a clean fresh copy, then arranges fake return addresses on its desk so any inspector checking who called a sensitive action sees only harmless routine clerk steps. Running inside wermgr.exe, the STEALTHVECTOR stage (analyzed by Elastic Security Labs) reads a clean copy of C:\Windows\System32\ntdll.dll from disk and overwrites the .text code section of the already-loaded ntdll.dll in RAM (because user-mode EDR agents monitor a program by placing 5-byte JMP "wiretap" hooks at the start of system functions inside ntdll.dll in memory, so pasting the clean bytes from disk right over the hooked bytes erases all of the EDR’s user-mode wiretaps). Simultaneously, it constructs synthetic thread call-stack frames (RtlUserThreadStart → BaseThreadInitThunk, so EDR memory walkers see a normal Windows call stack instead of unbacked shellcode) and ChaCha20/AES-GCM-decrypts Mandiant’s DUSTTRAP backdoor directly in memory. To unhook ntdll.dll, STEALTHVECTOR calls VirtualProtect on the in-memory ntdll.dll .text section (temporarily changing it from Read-Execute 0x20 to Read-Write-Execute 0x40), copies the clean .text bytes from the on-disk ntdll.dll file, and restores 0x20 permissions, silencing user-mode API hooks before DUSTTRAP initializes. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ STACK SPOOF + RX / ⇠#2 ALERT 312 KB RX) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Signed Host Binary (taskhost.exe)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Elastic Defend & ETW Ti Sensor).

stages.title: CLOUDFLARE WORKER C2 & PLUGIN EXECUTION
stages.subtitle: DUSTTRAP loads modular plugins and beacons over TLS 1.3
stages.description: With every hallway monitor blinded and its footsteps disguised, the implant unfolds sixteen specialized espionage modules purely inside live memory and establishes a mutually authenticated encrypted radio link straight back to its remote handlers. With ntdll.dll unhooked inside wermgr.exe, the DUSTTRAP core opens a mutual-TLS channel (requiring both client and server certificates so security researchers cannot probe the C2 server or replay traffic) to APT41’s command infrastructure, and loads 16 specialized in-memory plugins (file manager, shell executor, credential harvester, Active Directory recon, streamed into RAM only when needed so the full toolkit never sits on the victim’s hard drive). Although unhooking ntdll.dll blinds user-mode API hooks inside wermgr.exe, Kernel-mode Event Tracing for Windows (EtwTiLogProtectVM) and Sysmon EventID 3 still catch the ntdll.dll permission change paired with wermgr.exe connecting to a non-Microsoft IP address. In the documented Sysmon EID 3 exchange from Signed Host Binary (taskhost.exe) to DodgeBox Stack-Spoofing & DUSTTRAP, DodgeBox Stack-Spoofing & DUSTTRAP responds with ACK TLS 1.3 (confirming that the WORKER TLS C2 request succeeded on DodgeBox Stack-Spoofing & DUSTTRAP and completing the final execution objective of Elastic & Mandiant, APT41 (Brass Typhoon): DodgeBox, Call-Stack Spoofing & DUSTPAN Loader). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ WORKER TLS C2 / ⇠#3 ACK TLS 1.3) from Node ③ (#3 Signed Host Binary (taskhost.exe)) to Node ④ (#4 DodgeBox Stack-Spoofing & DUSTTRAP), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Elastic Defend & ETW Ti Sensor).

detectionRule.title: Relocated System Binary Side-Loading Unsigned DLL from ProgramData
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: APT41 DodgeBox / DUSTPAN DLL Side-Loading Pattern
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|startswith: 'C:\ProgramData\'
    Signed: 'false'
  condition: selection
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Audit and block execution of Windows system binaries relocated outside C:\Windows\System32\.

detectionRule.title: APT41 DodgeBox / DUSTPAN Reflective Loader Signature
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule APT41_DodgeBox_Dustpan_Loader {
  meta:
    author = "Elastic Security Labs / Mandiant"
    actor = "APT41 (Brass Typhoon)"
  strings:
    $chacha = "expand 32-byte k" ascii
    $api1 = "RtlLookupFunctionEntry" ascii
    $api2 = "NtAllocateVirtualMemory" ascii
  condition:
    uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and all of them
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Inspect thread call-stacks where return addresses point to instructions not preceded by a valid CALL opcode (call-stack spoofing detection).

detectionRule.title: System Binary Connecting to Serverless Worker C2 Domains
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Outbound Connection to Serverless Worker Domain
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - '.workers.dev'
      - '.pages.dev'
    Image|startswith: 'C:\ProgramData\'
  condition: selection
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Restrict server egress via proxy allowlists and inspect TLS SNI headers for unauthorized *.workers.dev connections.
